title: Priority Inkblot: company OKR → initiative traceability catalog and escalation paths
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales to more Dedicated/Private customers and parallel initiatives, leadership and engineers report friction when mapping company-level OKRs to the concrete set of team deliverables. Current artifacts are fragmented: spreadsheets, ad-hoc Confluence pages, and project boards that drift. This causes late detection of scope gaps, duplicated work, and slow escalation when an initiative misses a critical milestone.

Goal: Create a canonical "Priority Inkblot" traceability catalog and an operational escalation path that makes it trivial to answer: which initiatives directly map to a company-level Key Result, what are the leading indicators for each mapping, who owns the handoff, and where to route blockers. The artifact should be machine-readable and integrated with existing tools (Linear, Confluence, GitHub, and Console dashboards).

Scope: Catalog design (schema + UX), automation to sync Linear issues to the catalog, a rollout playbook for PM/Eng/Design leads, and a lightweight escalation runbook for missed milestones. Deliverables: 1) Traceability catalog spec (Confluence PRD), 2) a shared Confluence index + JSON export, 3) two automation scripts: Linear→catalog sync and daily gap detector, 4) a one-pager escalation flow and on-call contact mapping.

Non-goals: This ticket does not build a full orchestration system for OKR-driven portfolio management or replace the roadmap tool; it provides a canonical mapping layer and pragmatic integrations that live alongside existing toolsets.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical catalog schema (JSON) is reviewed and approved by PM, Eng, Design
At least 80% of company-level OKRs have explicit initiative mappings in the catalog
Two-way sync from Linear root issues to catalog entries successfully runs in staging daily
The gap detector flags missing leading indicators for mapped Key Results and sends summary to exec-integrations@redwood.ai
Escalation runbook validated with two cross-functional leads and merged to Confluence
work_items: Draft catalog schema with fields: okr_id, okr_title, kr_id, initiative_key, initiative_title, owner, leading_indicators, downstream_tasks, dependencies, risk_level, mitigations, status, last_updated
Prototype Confluence spec and UI wireframe for the catalog index
Implement Linear→catalog sync (serverless job) with stubbed auth and ID mapping
Build gap detector that compares OKR targets to initiative leading indicators and produces weekly report
Run two walkthroughs: PM all-hands and Eng triage to validate use cases
Publish escalation runbook and onboard first responders

risks: Sync reliability: Linear rate limits or schema drift could cause missing entries
Adoption: teams may not keep mappings up to date without clear owner incentives
Surface level: Over-simplifying leading indicators could create false confidence
mitigations: Build idempotent sync with backfills and an audit log
Add catalog ownership to quarterly PM/Eng reviews and tie to roadmap sign-offs
Flag low-confidence mappings in the catalog and surface them in the weekly report
rollout_plan: Week 1: schema sign-off + staging sync runs (PM + Eng)
Week 2: runbook and gap detector enabled; pilot with Infra and Console teams
Week 3: wider PM org onboarding and executive summary email automation
Week 4: iterate on UX and add links to Console OKR dashboard
